$comment: SSOT for the zone-id format. Every consumer derives its rules from this
file rather than restating them: the Rust validator is generated from it at
compile time (rust/contracts/build.rs -> OUT_DIR, never committed), and
non-Rust consumers generate from the same file.
Prose describing this format already existed in several places and matched
no implementation, because nothing enforced it. The point of this file is
that there is now exactly one place to change it.
Reserved ids are listed by the constant that owns them, not by value:
rust/contracts/src/constants.rs is the SSOT for what those strings are.

length.why: DNS-label bounds. Zone ids appear in hostnames and certificate SANs; anything a label cannot carry is unusable there.

charset.why: Lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphen. Case is excluded rather than folded: two ids differing only in case would be one zone in DNS and two on disk.

edges.why: A leading or trailing hyphen is not a valid DNS label.

reserved.why: Tenant-creatable ids must not collide with zones the kernel owns. CONTROL_ZONE_ID is additionally unspellable under the charset rule above, which is deliberate; ROOT_ZONE_ID is not, so it needs this list.

mutability.why: The id is the first path segment of everything in the zone, so renaming is not renaming. Changing --cluster-init from one id to another on a live deployment created a fresh empty zone and abandoned the old one, with no error at any layer (observed 2026-09-09).
